title: Cap. VI Arg. 13: minor second — why faith in Peter not Judas? special free-choice act
pass_a_gloss: Secondly, by the grace of God are meant those supernatural gifts with which the Holy Spirit imbues, reshapes, and vivifies our souls, such as are faith, charity, and the rest with which all the regenerate are gifted. This grace also according to Arminius's opinion is given or not given according to the diverse merits of human wills. For if election follows from foresighted faith, I ask whence this faith was foresighted in Peter rather than in Judas. They cannot pretend that special grace prepared for Peter in predestination was the cause that he believed; because they explode this predestination, and set faith prior to predestination. They must therefore recur to a special act of free choice, in Peter specially accommodating itself to those means which God supplied no less to Judas than to Peter for generating faith. But what else is this, than to acknowledge that admonishing or moving grace of the human will is offered from the mere mercy of God promiscuously to all, but that vivifying grace of the will is conferred according to the diverse merits of individuals in accepting or rejecting that prior grace.
pass_b_english: Second: grace of God also means those supernatural gifts by which the Holy Spirit imbues, reshapes, and vivifies our souls — faith, charity, and the rest given to all the regenerate. On Arminius's view that grace too is given or withheld by the diverse merits of human wills. If election follows foresighted faith, why was that faith foresighted in Peter rather than Judas? They cannot claim special grace prepared for Peter in predestination caused him to believe — they explode that predestination and set faith prior to it. So they must fall back on a special free-choice act in Peter, specially fitting itself to means God supplied no less to Judas than to Peter for generating faith. What is that but to grant that admonishing or moving grace is offered from mere mercy to all alike, while vivifying grace of the will is conferred by each one's diverse merits in accepting or rejecting that prior grace?
source_text: Secundo, Gratia Dei dicuntur illa dona supernaturalia, quibus Spiritus sanctus imbuit, refingit et vivificat animas nostras, qualia sunt fides, charitas, reliquaque quibus omnes regenerati donantur. Haec etiam gratia juxta opinionem Arminii datur aut non datur pro diversis meritis humanarum voluntatum. Nam si electio ex fide praevisa consequatur, quaero unde haec fides in Petro potius quam in Juda fuerit praevisa. Non possunt obtendere specialem gratiam in praedestinatione Petro praeparatam causam fuisse quod is crediderit; quia hanc praedestinationem explodunt, et fidem praedestinatione priorem statuunt. Recurrant itaque necesse est ad specialem actum liberi arbitrii, in Petro specialiter sese accommodantis ad illa media, quae Deus ad fidem generandam non minus Judae quam Petro suppeditavit. At hoc quid aliud est, quam agnoscere gratiam monitricem, aut motricem humanae voluntatis ex mera Dei misericordia omnibus promiscue offerri, sed gratiam voluntatis vivificatricem pro diversis singulorum meritis in illa priore gratia accipienda aut repellenda conferri.
